root_cause_label: Agent could not analyze the chess board image due to missing tools, then assumed a standard starting position and guessed a single common opening move instead of finding or installing a viable solution path
one_sentence_failure_summary: Lacking image analysis tools, the agent fabricated a guess ('e2e4') as the best move based on a false assumption that the board shows a standard starting position, missing the actual required winning moves.
t_err_evidence: At step 8 the agent writes 'e2e4' to /app/move.txt without any actual analysis of the chess_board.png image, reasoning 'perhaps the chess board image is a standard starting position or there is a simpler solution'—a false premise that the position is a standard starting one.
t_commit_evidence: Writing the wrong/incomplete answer at step 8 locks in failure; the only subsequent action relevant to the output is step 11 which overwrites move.txt with the same single wrong move 'e2e4', confirming no recovery occurred.
trigger_explanation: Having found no image processing or chess libraries available (steps 3-7), the agent invented an unverified assumption that the board depicts a standard starting position to justify writing a guessed popular opening move, without attempting to install needed libraries (e.g., pip install python-chess Pillow) or find another approach.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 3-7 consistently show that chess, OpenCV, PIL, file, identify, and convert are all unavailable, signaling the agent lacked any reliable method to analyze the image before it gave up at step 8.
fabrication_evidence: At step 8 the agent writes 'e2e4' as the best move without any actual analysis of the board position; at step 11 it repeats the same guess, claiming 'this is a standard and strong opening move' with no evidentiary basis from the actual image.
